tasks.title: Add ApiError variants and the api module scaffold
acceptance: `src/error.rs` gains `ApiError` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`) with at least the variants `Unauthorized`, `RateLimited { retry_after: Option<std::time::Duration> }`, `Server { status: u16 }`, `Transport { source }`, `Decode { source }`, `InsecureBaseUrl`, and `RetriesExhausted { attempts: u32 }`
`AppError` gains `Api(#[from] ApiError)` and renders it with an `api: ` prefix, matching the existing `Auth(..)` style
No `ApiError` variant can carry raw token material; a unit test formats every variant with `{}` and `{:?}` and asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` never appears
`ApiError` exposes `fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool` returning true for `Server`, `RateLimited` and `Transport` only (unit-tested per variant)
`src/api/mod.rs` exists with module docs and `#![allow(dead_code)]`-equivalent scoping like `src/auth/mod.rs`; `src/main.rs` declares `mod api;`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Follow the error conventions already set by `AuthError` in `src/error.rs` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`, crate-wide `Result<T> = Result<T, AppError>`). Do not touch the `Secret`/`REDACTED` helper in `src/log.rs`. No HTTP code in this task - only the error type and module wiring, so the rest of the epic can land in parallel.

tasks.title: Shared sync scalar types: ids, due and deadline objects
acceptance: `common.rs` defines serde `Deserialize`/`Serialize` types for the Sync API due object (`date`, `string`, `lang`, `is_recurring`, `timezone`) and deadline object (`date`, `lang`), each with `#[serde(default)]` on optional fields

A due `date` accepts both the date-only form (`2024-05-01`) and the floating/UTC datetime forms (`2024-05-01T10:00:00`, `2024-05-01T10:00:00Z`) and round-trips the original string without loss (unit test per form)
Every struct tolerates unknown JSON fields (no `deny_unknown_fields`); a unit test deserialises a due object containing an extra `"future_field": 1` key successfully
Priority is modelled as a type that maps the API's 1..=4 integers and rejects out-of-range values with a decode error, and ids are modelled as a `String`-backed newtype used by the later model tasks

`src/api/model/mod.rs` declares `pub mod common;` and re-exports the public types; `src/api/mod.rs` is NOT modified by this task beyond nothing - if a `pub mod model;` declaration is required, stop and report rather than editing files outside this list
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: These are the shapes every other resource embeds, so land them first. The epic flags due/deadline shapes as the main drift risk - keep fields `Option` and additive, never strict. Use plain `String` for timestamps (no chrono dependency in Cargo.toml); parsing into dates is a later epic's concern.

tasks.title: Domain structs for Project, Section, Label, Filter and User
acceptance: `Project` carries at least `id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `child_order`, `color`, `is_favorite`, `is_archived`, `is_deleted`, `view_style`; `Section` carries `id`, `name`, `project_id`, `section_order`, `is_deleted`, `is_archived`

`Label`, `Filter` and `User` carry `id`, `name`/`full_name`, order/color fields and `is_deleted` where the API provides it; `User` additionally keeps `tz_info` or equivalent timezone data as a tolerant nested struct

All structs derive `Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize`, use `#[serde(default)]` for optional fields and accept unknown fields without error (one unit test per struct feeding an extra `"x": null` key)
`is_deleted` deserialises from both JSON booleans and the legacy 0/1 integer form (unit-tested)
`src/api/model/mod.rs` declares and re-exports the five new modules
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Reuse the id/priority/colour helpers from `src/api/model/common.rs` (T-202) instead of redefining them. These structs are data only - no persistence, no business rules (EPIC-04 owns storage).

tasks.title: Domain structs for Item and Note
acceptance: `Item` carries at least `id`, `content`, `description`, `project_id`, `section_id`, `parent_id`, `child_order`, `priority`, `labels`, `due`, `deadline`, `checked`, `is_deleted`, `added_at`, `completed_at`, `user_id`, `responsible_uid`
`Note` carries `id`, `item_id`, `project_id`, `content`, `posted_at`, `is_deleted` and a tolerant optional `file_attachment` nested struct
`labels` defaults to an empty `Vec` when the key is absent and `checked`/`is_deleted` accept both boolean and 0/1 integer forms (unit-tested)

`due` and `deadline` use the shared types from `src/api/model/common.rs`; an item with `"due": null` and an item with a full recurring due object both deserialise with no field loss (unit test asserts every listed field round-trips)
Unknown JSON fields on `Item` and `Note` do not cause a decode error (unit test)
`src/api/model/mod.rs` declares and re-exports `item` and `note`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Runs in parallel with T-203; both edit `src/api/model/mod.rs`, so expect a trivial merge there. Items are the hottest struct in the app - keep it `Clone` and cheap, no owned client handles inside.

tasks.title: Sync request and response envelope types
acceptance: `SyncRequest` serialises `sync_token`, `resource_types` and `commands`; `SyncRequest::full()` sets `sync_token` to `"*"` and `resource_types` to exactly `["projects","items","sections","labels","notes","filters","user","day_orders"]`
A unit test serialises `SyncRequest::full()` to `serde_json::Value` and asserts the `resource_types` array equals that eight-element list exactly - no extra and no missing entries, order asserted
`commands` is omitted from the body when empty (`skip_serializing_if`), and an incremental constructor takes a caller-supplied sync token

`SyncResponse` deserialises `sync_token`, `full_sync`, `temp_id_mapping`, `sync_status`, `full_sync_date_utc` plus the resource arrays `projects`, `items`, `sections`, `labels`, `notes`, `filters`, `user`, `day_orders`; every array defaults to empty and `user` is optional
`sync_status` deserialises both the `"ok"` string form and the per-command error object form without failing; unknown top-level fields are ignored (unit test)
`src/api/mod.rs` declares `pub mod sync;` and `pub mod model;` and re-exports the envelope types
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: The eight resource types are a hard acceptance item of the epic - define them as a single `const RESOURCE_TYPES: [&str; 8]` so the test and the code read from the same source. `day_orders` is a map of project id to order; keep it as a tolerant `serde_json::Map`-backed type if the shape is uncertain rather than guessing.

tasks.title: Retry policy with exponential backoff, jitter and injectable clock
acceptance: `RetryPolicy` has configurable `max_attempts` (default bounded, e.g. 4), `base_delay`, `max_delay` and a jitter fraction; `delay_for_attempt(n)` grows exponentially and is clamped at `max_delay` (unit-tested for attempts 1..=6)
Jitter is injected through a trait/closure seam so a deterministic test double yields reproducible delays; with jitter disabled the delays are exactly `base * 2^(n-1)` capped at `max_delay`

A `Sleeper`/`Clock` trait abstracts waiting, with a tokio-backed impl for production and a recording test double that captures requested durations without sleeping; the unit tests use only the double (test suite stays under a second)

`retry(policy, clock, op)` re-runs an async operation while the returned `ApiError::is_retryable()` is true, stops after `max_attempts` with `ApiError::RetriesExhausted { attempts }`, and returns non-retryable errors (e.g. `Unauthorized`) immediately with zero recorded sleeps
When the error is `ApiError::RateLimited { retry_after: Some(d) }` the waited duration is at least `d`, overriding the computed backoff (unit test asserts the recorded duration >= 2s for a 2s hint)
`src/api/mod.rs` declares `pub mod retry;`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Parallel with the model tasks - depends only on `ApiError` from T-201. Keep this module HTTP-free and generic over the operation so the client in T-207 just wraps its request future. `rand` is not in Cargo.toml; derive jitter from an injected source (e.g. a `FnMut() -> f64` seam defaulting to a small nanotime-based scramble) rather than adding a dependency - if a dependency really is needed, stop and report.

tasks.title: SyncClient: HTTPS reqwest transport and status mapping
acceptance: `SyncClient::new(token: Token, base_url: &str) -> Result<Self>` builds one reused `reqwest::Client` with `https_only`, a connect timeout and a request timeout; a non-https base URL is rejected with `ApiError::InsecureBaseUrl` before any network activity (same debug-only loopback exception as `src/auth/validate.rs`)
`sync(&self, req: &SyncRequest) -> Result<SyncResponse>` POSTs to `{base}/api/v1/sync` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, JSON body, and decodes into `SyncResponse`

The token is read only via `Token::expose` when building the header; it never appears in the URL, in a log line or in any error - a unit test asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` is absent from the `Debug` of the client and of every error it can build

Status mapping: 401/403 -> `ApiError::Unauthorized`; 429 -> `ApiError::RateLimited` with `retry_after` parsed from the `Retry-After` header (delta-seconds form, `None` when absent/unparseable); 5xx -> `ApiError::Server { status }`; transport failure -> `ApiError::Transport`; body that fails to parse -> `ApiError::Decode`
`sync` runs the request through the T-206 retry helper, with the policy and clock injectable via a constructor/builder so tests can supply the recording double
`src/api/mod.rs` declares `pub mod client;` and re-exports `SyncClient`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Mirror the proven patterns in `src/auth/validate.rs`: injectable `base_url`, `is_acceptable_base_url_scheme`-style guard, named timeout constants, token read only through `Token::expose`. Unlike the validator, build the client once and keep it in the struct. No persistence, no queueing, no endpoints other than `/sync`.

tasks.title: Full-sync fixture and no-field-loss deserialisation test
acceptance: `tests/fixtures/sync_full.json` is a realistic full-sync response containing at least two projects, three items (one with a recurring due, one with a deadline, one completed/`checked`, one `is_deleted`), one section, one label, one note, one filter, the `user` object, `day_orders`, `temp_id_mapping`, `sync_status`, `full_sync: true` and `full_sync_date_utc`
The fixture contains only fake data - no real account ids, emails, phone numbers or tokens (ids are obviously synthetic, e.g. `6X4Vfake0001`, email `user@example.invalid`)

A test deserialises the fixture into `SyncResponse` and asserts, field by field, that every field listed in the EPIC-03 acceptance (`is_deleted`, `checked`, due, deadline, priority, labels, `parent_id`, `section_id`, `child_order`) survives with the expected value
The fixture additionally carries unknown keys at top level, inside an item and inside a due object; the test asserts deserialisation still succeeds (unknown-field tolerance)
A round-trip test re-serialises the decoded response and asserts no asserted field changed value
`cargo test --all` passes with no network access
tasks.context: Runs in parallel with T-206/T-207 since it only needs the envelope and model types. The epic flags fixture drift as a risk - add a short header comment in the JSON naming the API version (`/api/v1/sync`) and the date the shape was taken from docs.

tasks.title: Wiremock integration tests for retry, 429, 401 and request shape
acceptance: Request shape: a mock asserts the received body has `sync_token: "*"` and exactly the eight required `resource_types` (no extras), and that the `Authorization` header is `Bearer tok_fake_abc123`
Two mocked 500s followed by a 200 -> `sync` succeeds, the mock asserts exactly 3 received requests, and the recorded delays from the injected clock are strictly increasing

Mocked 429 with `Retry-After: 2` then 200 -> the first recorded delay is >= 2s and the test completes in well under 2s of wall clock (no real sleeping; asserted via the injected clock double from T-206)
Mocked 401 -> `ApiError::Unauthorized` is returned immediately and the mock asserts exactly 1 received request
Mocked 200 whose JSON body contains unknown fields at top level and inside resources -> `sync` returns `Ok` (no decode error); a malformed body (`{`) -> `ApiError::Decode`
Persistent 500s -> `ApiError::RetriesExhausted { attempts }` with the attempt count equal to the policy's `max_attempts`, asserted against the mock's request count
All tests use fake tokens only, make no real network calls, and `cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: `wiremock = "0.6"` is already a dev-dependency (added for T-106); follow the mock setup style used by the `wiremock_tests` module in `src/auth/validate.rs`. Point the client at the mock server's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` URL, which is accepted in debug builds by the loopback exception. The fixture from T-208 can be reused as the 200 body.

tasks.title: Document the sync client contract and fixture-drift procedure
acceptance: Documents the request contract: endpoint `POST /api/v1/sync`, the eight resource types and why the list is fixed, `sync_token: "*"` for full sync vs. a stored token for incremental

Documents the error taxonomy (`Unauthorized`, `RateLimited`, `Server`, `Transport`, `Decode`, `RetriesExhausted`), which are retried and which are not, and the backoff/jitter parameters with their defaults
Contains a reproducible procedure for refreshing `tests/fixtures/sync_full.json` against a live account, including the rule that all ids/emails must be scrubbed to fake values before committing

States what is explicitly out of scope for this epic (persistence, queueing, conflict handling, quick-add and completed-tasks endpoints pending open questions 1 and 3) and that `src/auth/validate.rs` remains a minimal token check superseded by this client
Uses only fake tokens and synthetic ids; markdown links resolve
